properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised by @ajs on 2026-09-13 as part of the seed-template idea — "then a domain expert can develop and review templates for specific domains." Recorded separately because it has a different failure mode from the template idea itself, and it is the one that would sink it.

THE PROBLEM. A template's selling point is that it carries a field's current practice, standards, codes and regulations. Every one of those things CHANGES. And the user a template is FOR — @ajs's own words, "somebody designing in a domain that they are not the expert in" — is precisely the person who cannot tell a current practice from a superseded one. A blank graph is honestly empty; a stale template is confidently wrong, and it is wearing a domain expert's authority while being so.

HIS OWN ANSWER, which is the right shape and does not finish the job: a domain expert develops and reviews the template. That settles who AUTHORS it. It does not settle:
 · how a design created from template v3 learns that v5 exists
 · whether a seeded node keeps pointing at the template it came from, or is absorbed and forgotten
 · what happens when a standard is superseded AFTER a design was seeded — does anything tell the design, or does it quietly keep asserting a withdrawn code?
 · whether "reviewed by a domain expert" is a claim the graph can hold and check, or just prose in a README

⭐ THIS DESIGN HAS ALREADY BEEN BITTEN BY THE GENERAL SHAPE, TWICE TODAY, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN ASSUMING: `fact:a-retired-dependencys-facts-keep-describing-this-project` records a fact whose subject was retired and which went on reading as current — it misled two readers 16 days apart. A seeded design is that hazard at scale: dozens of nodes asserting a world that was true when the template was written.

📌 AND THERE IS AN EXISTING MECHANISM THAT ALMOST FITS. reflow2 already has `mirrors` — "I designed against your published surface, pinned at this version" — built and, measured on 2026-08-13, never used once. A template is arguably the same relationship: a design pinned against a published thing that can move. Whether that machinery is the answer here, or only looks like it, is not established.

⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT BE ASSUMED: that reflow2 should VALIDATE a template's content. Judging whether a template states the correct standards for a domain is a domain-expert act, and reflow2's standing posture is report-don't-judge. The question here is whether it can carry and track a warrant, not whether it can issue one.
properties.name: OPEN — who WARRANTS a domain template, and how does a design know its seed has gone stale? A template carries authority, which is exactly what makes an out-of-date one dangerous
properties.rationale: Split out from the main template idea because the two fail differently and can be answered separately: one asks whether templates should exist, this asks what makes one trustworthy over time. Recorded as a brainstorm — @ajs was thinking out loud and stated no preference.
